title: Acid-base equilibria: Kz, Kb, Kw and buffers - 123 school
heading: Acid-base equilibria: Kz, Kb, Kw and buffers
intro: Choose the correct answer for each question. Use a calculator where needed.

questions.question: What is the equilibrium condition of HZ + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup> + Z<sup>–</sup>?
What is the equilibrium condition of NH<sub>3</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> + OH<sup>–</sup>?
What is the value of K<sub>w</sub> at 298 K?
Which equation is correct at 298 K?
Which relationship holds for an acid and its conjugate base?
An acid has K<sub>z</sub> = 1.0·10<sup>–5</sup>. What is K<sub>b</sub> of the conjugate base?
Acid A has K<sub>z</sub> = 1.0·10<sup>–3</sup>, acid B has K<sub>z</sub> = 1.0·10<sup>–6</sup>. What is true?

answers.c: A and B are equally strong

questions.question: What is the difference between a strong and a weak acid?

answers.a: a strong acid has an equilibrium and a weak acid does not
answers.b: a strong acid is always concentrated
answers.d: a strong acid reacts (almost) completely with water, a weak acid only partly

questions.question: What is the pH of 0.10 mol/L HCl?
What is the pH of 0.010 mol/L NaOH?
What is the pH of 0.10 mol/L of a weak acid with K<sub>z</sub> = 1.0·10<sup>–5</sup>?
What is the pH of 0.10 mol/L acetic acid (K<sub>z</sub> = 1.7·10<sup>–5</sup>)?
A solution has pH = 3.00. What is [H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>]?
What is the pH of 0.10 mol/L of a weak base with K<sub>b</sub> = 1.0·10<sup>–5</sup>?
You dilute a solution of a weak acid 100 times. What approximately happens to the pH?

answers.b: the pH becomes 100 times as large

questions.question: You dilute a solution of a strong acid 100 times. What happens to the pH?
What is a buffer?

answers.b: a solution of a strong acid
answers.c: a solution that does not react with acids and bases
answers.d: a solution whose pH hardly changes when you add a little acid or base

questions.question: Which mixture is a buffer?
You add a little acid to an acetic acid / acetate buffer. What reacts with the added H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>?
You add a little base to an acetic acid / acetate buffer. What reacts with the added OH<sup>–</sup>?
Which system keeps the pH of blood almost constant at about 7.4?
What is the conjugate base of acetic acid (CH<sub>3</sub>COOH)?
A buffer contains as much HZ as Z<sup>–</sup>. For HZ, K<sub>z</sub> = 1.0·10<sup>–5</sup>. What is the pH?
When does a buffer no longer work?

answers.c: when one of the two components of the buffer is used up

questions.question: Which acid is stronger: acetic acid (K<sub>z</sub> = 1.7·10<sup>–5</sup>) or NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> (K<sub>z</sub> = 5.6·10<sup>–10</sup>)?

answers.a: acetic acid, because K<sub>z</sub> is larger
